title: Arabic: Read Arabic in Latin characters

blocks.text: In the messages, comments and posts, millions of people write dialect with Latin letters and figures:3amel eh?.......................................7abibis. It is Arabic ( ⁧عَرَبِيزِي⁩ , born with the first mobile phones without Arabic keyboard and remained alive especially among young people, in Egypt, the Levant, the Gulf and the Maghreb. For those working on open sources is a frequent obstacle: a comment in Arabic is not found looking in Arabic characters, and a figure can be a letter. In this unit learn the code (what they mean 2, 3, 5, 7...), the main regional variants, the most common abbreviations and the method to transcribe a message into Arabic in Arabic characters and understand it. Unity is of understanding: it does not ask you to write in Arabic, but to read it. Five weeks, in parallel with B2-11, B2-12 and INT-04.

rows: 7–8 hours · five weeks (weeks 199–203), about 1,5 hours per week

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner for reading aloud
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. read the Arabic letters figures and combinations and link them to the Arabic letters;
2. transcribe a short message into Egyptian Arabic characters and translate it;
3. recognize the main Levantine, Gulf and Maghrebine variants;
4. understand the most common abbreviations, English and French words and emojis;
5. avoid typical reading errors (exchanged figures, ambiguous vowels, foreign words).
Five-week plan (a block from 60 minutes and one by 30 per week).

blocks.text: Emotional letters. ⁧ص⁩ , ⁧ض⁩ , ⁧ط⁩ , ⁧ظ⁩ they often write as s, d, t, z simple (sa7, dahr, tayeb, zabt), especially in Egypt. The context and the whole word say if it's emphatic: "tayeb" = ⁧طيب⁩ It's okay.

Vowels. Arabic follows pronunciation, not Arabic scripture: the same word can have more graphs. How are you doing? (m.) in Egyptian: ezayak, ezzayak, ezayk, izzayak. Long vowels are written with the simple vowel, doubled or with a combination: ʾawi = awi, 2awy, 2awii; Small ṣuġayyar = so3'ayar, sugar.
ā a · aa sabah, Sabaa7
Regional variants.

Recognize the origin. The figures used (2 for ⁧ق⁩ → Egypt; 8 or g per ⁧ق⁩ → Gulf; for ⁧ش⁩ → Maghreb or Lebanon) and spy words (baddi, halla2 → Levante; shlonak, wayed → Gulf; bezzaf, daba → Maghreb) is often enough to understand where the author writes. It is not a test: people travel and imitate themselves.
